_proves: The 2026-08-03 silent miss, pinned. Before the button-pair detector both questions below were absent from `fields` entirely: their controls are plain <button>s with no aria state, so the button loop filed all four in `btns` with r:"other" — a list fill-plan.mjs never reads — and the plan never mentioned either question. Two tiers are visible here in one scan: the recognised Yes/No set becomes a real radio group (fillable from an exact bank hit, still governed by the confirm-widget gate), and the three-option pronouns set becomes a verb-less widget (reported, blocking, never acted on).

heading: Full-Stack Engineer

fields.l: Will you now or in the future require sponsorship for employment visa status?
fields._note: TIER 2. A recognised closed answer set, so the pair travels as what it is and the banked answer rides onto the defer with it. `req` comes from the * in the label, which sits outside the question sentence — the question `l` carries is the sentence, not the marker.

o._note: No `sel`: the real board gives these buttons no id, name or data-testid — the only distinguishing attribute is a build-hashed class. The plan falls back to the data-aj stamp. No `on` either: the selected one is marked by that same hashed class, which is not a signal, so the scanner reports nothing rather than a guess.

fields._widget_note: SET ON THE RECOGNISED TIER TOO. fill-engine.mjs's kindOf() answers "forbidden:button", so no verb here can operate this control whatever `t` says. The key is what makes fill-plan.mjs route this to a confirm-widget defer carrying the resolved value and pick, instead of an items entry the engine would refuse and the report would call ticked.

fields._note: TIER 1. Three options, so not a recognised closed set. `t` is a type fill-plan.mjs's VERB map has no entry for, which lands it in the `unsupported field type` defer: reported, blocking, never acted on. Reporting is not a verb.
fields.labelWhy: answered by buttons whose answer set this scanner does not recognise

fields.l: Check Yes or No to indicate whether you have previously worked for Fixture Compute in any role.
fields._note: TIER 2, INSTRUCTION-PHRASED (2026-08-21). No "?" anywhere — the question is an imperative sentence, which is how Ashby words its texting consent. questionIn() alone left this pair to the widget sweep, which reported two separate fields labelled "Yes" and "No" on the live Quora and Flock Safety forms. The firstSentence fallback adopts it, gated on the answer set being CLOSED: a Yes/No pair under a sentence is a question; a Bold/Italic toolbar is not, and stays out of `fields`. The inner "Yes or No" survives because withoutOptions removes only the LAST occurrence of each option label — the buttons' own text, not the question's words. `req` comes from the * marker outside the sentence, exactly as g1 — required, so an UNKNOWN resolution DEFERS rather than skip-itemising.
